title: Your Own Type Traits Library
hints: Every trait is the same trick: a general template with the "no" answer, and a partial specialisation that matches the special shape (`const T`, `T*`, `T&`) with the "yes" answer (lesson 11.02).
`conditional<B, T, F>` has `using type = T;` in general and a specialisation for `false` with `using type = F;`.
requirements: In `namespace my`: `is_same`, `remove_const`, `remove_reference`, `is_pointer` and `conditional`, each with the `_v` or `_t` helper
A `static_assert` block testing each one against its `std::` version
A function template that uses one of your traits with `if constexpr` to behave differently for pointers
stretch: `decay`, and a detection trait `has_size<T>` that is true when `t.size()` compiles.
